title: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 Puts 1,000 Startups in Front of Global Investors
excerpt: The November 17-19 summit expects 60,000 visitors and 700 speakers, with a Startup Pavilion, Investor Connect matchmaking and a new AI and robotics pavilion.
body:
• The 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit runs November 17-19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre under the theme 'AI & Beyond'.
  • Organisers expect more than 60,000 business visitors, 25,000 delegates, 1,800 exhibitors and 700 speakers from over 75 countries.
  • More than 1,000 startups from 100 cities will exhibit at the Startup Pavilion, with a three-day Investor Connect programme, pitching arena and one-on-one mentoring.
  • For founders: the actionable core is Investor Connect matchmaking and the two startup stages — register through the official summit site before travelling.

The Bengaluru Tech Summit returns for its 29th edition from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre, with artificial intelligence at the centre of the programme and startups at the centre of the floor. Organised by the Karnataka government's Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, the summit is billed as Asia's largest integrated technology event. The state announced the edition earlier this year, as reported by The Hindu BusinessLine.

The scale

Organisers expect more than 60,000 business visitors, over 25,000 delegates, more than 1,800 exhibitors and over 700 speakers across more than 120 sessions, with participation from over 75 countries and more than 30 Indian states and Union Territories. The floor will include more than 20 country pavilions and over 175 international exhibitors. The programme spans 18 thematic tracks, including IT and deeptech, frontier technologies, electronics and semiconductors, electric mobility, health and biotech, data centres, cybersecurity, global capability centres, fintech and the orange economy, plus a dedicated India-USA Tech Conclave. A new AI and Robotics Pavilion, spanning more than 50,000 square feet, is planned with live demonstrations of humanoids, drones and autonomous systems, with nearly 101 robotics and drone startups expected to participate. The inaugural embedded world India, focused on electronics and semiconductors, will also debut at this edition.

What startups get

The Startup Pavilion will host more than 1,000 startups, incubators and accelerators from 100 cities, including cohorts from the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission's 'Beyond Bengaluru' initiative and the Software Technology Parks of India's 'Sayuj' programme. Eighteen sector pavilions group startups across AI, agritech, direct-to-consumer, fintech, semiconductors, robotics and SaaS. Two startup stages — 'Deeptech For Business' and 'Consumer Tech For Billions' — will run workshops on go-to-market strategy, investor readiness, product management, cybersecurity and AI. The three-day Investor Connect Programme offers curated, sector-specific matchmaking between startups, investors and corporates, a pitching arena in front of global venture capital firms, a reverse-pitching session in which investors present their theses, and one-on-one mentoring with entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and domain experts, according to the preview in Inc42.

Who is speaking

Announced speakers include Sandeep Sahai, chief executive of Clearwater Analytics; Vivek Raghavan, co-founder of Sarvam AI; V. Anantha Nageswaran, chief economic adviser to the Government of India; Ranjani Mani, director and country head for generative AI at Microsoft; Rangesh Raghavan of Lam Research; Sowmya Swaminathan of the M S Swaminathan Research Foundation; and Velislava Petrova-Chamova, Bulgaria's minister of foreign affairs. Sponsors and partners include Infosys, Biocon, QpiAI, Bosch Global Software Technologies, Qualcomm, Intel, SAP, eBay, Applied Materials, Fujitsu and Cloudflare, alongside trade bodies from Sweden, Italy, Australia and Poland. The Future Makers Conclave will felicitate Indian startups that entered the unicorn club since the last edition and mark 10 years of Karnataka's Elevate programme.

The context

Karnataka accounts for 42% of India's IT exports and leads the country in software exports, biotechnology and aerospace and defence manufacturing. Bengaluru ranks 15th among global startup ecosystems and 12th among the world's largest technology talent hubs. For diaspora founders and investors travelling in for the summit, the commercial centre of gravity is the investor programme rather than the keynotes: three days of pre-matched meetings in one venue, in a city where a large share of India's technology decisions are made.
